find: export const TEAM_COLORS: readonly [number, number, number] = [0xff3b3b, 0xfcc0fc, 0x4eff3b];
replace: export const TEAM_COLORS: readonly [number, number, number] = [0xff3b3b, 0xfcc0fc, 0xffffff];
why: Team C loses its own hue and renders as the white fallback -- the state that shipped between issue #281's descriptor landing and TEAM_COLORS gaining a third entry. It is not a crash and not a blank: `teamColor` still returns a colour, the ring still draws, the shell still tints, the tread trail still blends, and the stock chip still paints. What is lost is that a 2v1v1 match renders one whole SIDE in the fallback white, which the player has no way to read as a team. Deliberately mutated to `0xffffff` -- the actual fallback -- rather than to a duplicate of team A or B: a duplicate is caught by the pairwise-distinctness sweep, which makes that the easy half, while the fallback is a DISTINCT colour and passes every distinctness assertion. It is caught instead by the stock-readout case that asserts team 2's chip is TEAM_COLORS[2] and is not the fallback, which is the one place the two are told apart. Scoped to entities.test.ts and hud.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only. RE-ANCHORED for issue #579, which re-picked team B from #3b82ff to #fcc0fc: this entry names the whole TEAM_COLORS line, so the colour change turned it into FAILED-TO-APPLY -- a guard that stopped guarding, reported by the sweep and by nothing else. That is now the third entry in one session killed by a value it was anchored on (see `quad-board-loses-its-mirror-symmetry` and the two egress killedBy moves), which is an argument for anchoring on the SHAPE of a line rather than its contents wherever a mutation can express itself that way.
killedBy: hud: in-match stock readout (spec §3a, owner addition 2026-08-21) carries the TEAM as a letter beside the colour, all three teams (issue #281)
